The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). Never skip this because a daily timer already ran — the daily timer isn't synced to the moment you're about to change something. - **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss` reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one, a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account for. "Automatic" covers the routine, expected path; it does not mean an unexpected destructive step gets waved through. - **Anything outside the build/deploy/promote workflow is still stop-and-ask** — touching customer credentials, hand-editing `/opt/nxeon` outside the sanctioned scripts, restarting a service those scripts don't themselves restart, or touching any of the `/opt/nxeon-*` siblings that belong to other sessions. The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next` with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Read the PNG back and actually look at it — a sliced game wordmark, a clipped top bar and an empty Mods tab were all invisible in the code and obvious in a screenshot. ## Things that have already cost hours here - **Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls.** Always `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && …`. - **`git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks.** Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`. - **`git bundle create f A..B` with two raw SHAs** makes a bundle with no refs, which git refuses as empty. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

Rename path `lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts:366-436` does the same pre-check. So it fails gracefully, not a raw P2002 crash (though the `@unique` is still there as a backstop for races).

**2. Paid game servers** — field `Server.subdomain String? @unique` (schema.prisma:619, comment at 613-618 explicitly noting it must be cross-checked against `FreeMinecraftServer.subdomain`). Order flow: `lib/game-order.ts:295-314` — format-validates via shared `validateSubdomainFormat`, calls the same `isSubdomainAvailable(sub)` (line 313), throws a friendly `GameOrderError` if taken. On the actual `db.server.create` inside the tx (~line 550-580), a residual race is caught explicitly: `lib/game-order.ts:589-591` catches Prisma `P2002` and rethrows as `GameOrderError("That subdomain was just taken — go back and pick another.")` — graceful, not a 500.

**3. Shared hosting** — no `HostingAccount.subdomainLabel` DB column; hosting instead writes into a single cross-cutting registry `HostingHostnameClaim` with `hostname` unique across ALL hostname kinds (primary domain / subdomain / addon), documented at schema.prisma:1741-1753 (`primaryDomain has no unique` on its own, by design — the claim table is the real guard). Order flow `lib/actions-hosting.ts:225-251` (`orderHostingAccountFor`): builds `name = freeSubdomainFor(label)`, pre-checks `isHostnameClaimed(name)` (lines 244, 250) and returns a clean error; the atomic guard is `UNIQUE(hostname)` claimed inside the same DB transaction as account creation (comments at lines 158, 330-331). **This IS wired to a real-time client check**: `checkHostingSubdomain` (`lib/actions-hosting.ts:734-750`) is a server action called from `components/customer/HostingDeployWizard.tsx:355` inside a 400ms-debounced `useEffect` (lines 336-362) — as-you-type availability with "checking…"/"taken" states.

**4. Cross-collision gap — NOT real, already closed.** `lib/game-subdomain.ts:16-31` (`isSubdomainAvailable`) explicitly queries **both** `db.freeMinecraftServer.findFirst` and `db.server.findFirst` in parallel and requires both to miss. Both `actions-free-minecraft.ts:117` and `game-order.ts:313` call this same shared function — so free-MC and paid-game names are already checked against each other, both at pre-check and (per the doc comment on `Server.subdomain`, schema.prisma:613-618) intentionally coupled. Real-time UI check** exists **only for shared hosting** (`HostingDeployWizard.tsx:336-362` → `checkHostingSubdomain`), and only in the older `components/customer/` wizard — the newer Nexion wizard (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, `components/nx/order.tsx`) has **no** debounced/on-blur check wired for `o.subdomainLabel`, and neither Minecraft path (free or paid, `o.subdomain` in `order.tsx`) has any client-side call to `isSubdomainAvailable` anywhere in `components/`.
